subject: Language Usage
aligned_to: NWEA MAP Growth Language Usage goal areas (Writing: Write, Revise Texts for Purpose and Audience; Language: Understand, Edit for Grammar, Usage; Language: Understand, Edit for Mechanics) and RIT bands
note: All drafts and questions are original practice material written for this school. They are not NWEA test items.

units.title: Plan and Organize: Topic Sentences, Order and Transitions
skills: Choose a topic sentence that tells the main idea
Put steps and events in order
Use transition words (first, next, then, finally)
Take out a sentence that does not belong
vocab: the sentence that tells the main idea
what the writing is mostly about
a fact or example that tells more about the main idea
a word such as first, next or finally that connects ideas
the way sentences follow one after another
the ending that wraps up the writing

passage.title: Our Class Garden
passage.intro: Maha wrote about her class garden. Read her draft and answer the questions.
paras: (1) Our class has a small garden behind the school. (2) First, we pulled out all the weeds. (3) Then we dug small holes in the soil. (4) My cousin has a red bike. (5) Next, we put a bean seed in each hole. (6) We water the garden every morning. (7) Now little green plants are growing!

items.stem: Which sentence does NOT belong in the draft?
items.skill: Identifies a sentence that does not belong

items.stem: Maha wants to add this sentence: “We covered each seed with soil.” Where should it go?
items.skill: Puts sentences or events in a logical order

items.stem: Which word or phrase could BEST begin sentence 6?
items.skill: Chooses a transition that connects ideas

items.stem: Which word BEST replaces “put” in sentence 5 to make it more exact?
items.skill: Chooses precise or vivid language

items.stem: Which sentence would BEST begin the draft and tell the main idea?
options: Our class worked together to plant a garden.
My cousin likes to ride after school.
Beans can be green, yellow, white or purple.
Some schools have a big playground.
items.skill: Chooses a topic sentence that introduces the main idea

items.stem: Which sentence would be the BEST ending for the draft?
options: My cousin’s red bike is very fast and new.
Some people do not like to eat beans at all.
We cannot wait to pick our beans this spring!
First, we pulled out all of the weeds again.
items.skill: Chooses an effective concluding sentence

passage.intro: Nawaf is writing a report about camels. Read his draft and answer the questions.
paras: (1) Camels are amazing desert animals. (2) They can walk for many days without drinking water. (3) Their wide feet help them walk on soft sand. (4) Camels have long eyelashes. (5) I like camels a lot. (6) Many people in the desert still ride camels.

passage.intro: Yara is writing about a healthy snack. Read her draft and answer the questions.
